subject: Medford High School Building Project Options
overview: The Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee hosted a community forum to present six narrowed design alternatives and timeline requirements ahead of selecting a single preferred option for MSBA submission. The project team and district leaders answered public questions regarding construction phasing, MSBA reimbursement, athletic facilities, and the accommodation of non-high school programs.

items.title: Welcome and Purpose of Meeting
items.summary: Committee Chair Jenny Graham opened the forum, outlining the timeline leading to the June 10 decision to select a single preferred design option for the high school project.

items.title: MSBA Timeline and Deliverables
items.summary: Project representatives outlined the MSBA schedule, noting upcoming milestones including the June Preferred Schematic Report submission, board approvals, and a targeted local authorization vote in May 2027.

items.title: Deed Restrictions and Design Updates
items.summary: Architect Matt Rice explained modifications made to options C2.2 and C3.4 to avoid 1967 deed restrictions on Edgerly Field, the elimination of option D2.1, and the MSBA-requested development of a high-school-only program model.

items.title: Review of the Six Design Options and Cost Models
items.summary: The design team presented the six active alternatives—ranging from code upgrades and addition/renovations to all-new construction—reviewing their scope, phasing, baseline surface parking assumptions, and estimated costs.

items.title: Audience Q&A and Community Feedback
items.summary: Attendees asked questions about phasing impacts on occupied classrooms, escalation and estimating factors, auditorium capacity, field configurations, and the trade-offs of housing non-high school programs versus standalone alternatives.
